No voy a decirle a nadie que debe hacer, si quieren comprarlo, haganlo y experimenten, pero estoy 100% segura que perderan el dinero, mi hija tambien lo compro y me dijo exactamente lo mismo. title: Company Makes You Give 5 Stars to Get Replacement
text:
Initial Review- I really wanted to like these extensions. I have been a hair extension user for over two years. I am experienced in taking good care of my extensions. My favorite extension company recently raised their prices. I found these, LaaVoo, while looking for a similar but lower priced product. I was pleased with the quality of the hair when it arrived. The hair is real as described and the color was exactly what I wanted. The product arrived the 15th and 16th of September. I installed it on Saturday, September 18th. Installation went well. The first two weeks after installation everything was perfect. A little after 2 weeks I began to loose strands. The bonded tips (glue) were falling apart, the strand would fall out leaving the installation bead and the strand wire tip in my natural hair. I had half a pack left from my initial installation and I replaced the fallen strands with new ones. It has been approximately 6 weeks now and I have been replacing strands almost daily. More need replacing the more time goes by. I am very disappointed in how the product has held up. Other products have lasted me 3-4 months! I contacted LaaVoo Service Team using the information listed on their business card inside the product box. I explained the issue and they directed me back to amazon as that is where I bought them. The return window just closed and amazon can no longer help me. I am not happy and will not be purchasing again. If you want temporary extensions, these will do fine. If you're looking for a long lasting (3 months) quality product, this is not for you. (photo shows bonded tips that fell apart)
12/05/21 Update- Within a day or two of my initial review, I was contacted via amazon message service by the company. Remember, I initially contacted them for help and they denied me. The representative stated that they were eager to help but to do so I would need to email them using my private email. Very sneaky. This way amazon would not see that there are conditions of their "help". You must change your low rating to 5 stars and then you will get your replacement. I have saved all my emails from them in order to prove my statement. I had bought 3 packs, they sent me 1 replacement pack and 2 sets of mink eyelashes which I had said I didnt want. I used the replacement pack to replace the strands that fell out each week. The strand bonds continued to deteriorate and fall apart leaving the metal tip and bead in my hair after 2-3 weeks. I remain steadfast in my initial review. The hair seems to be of good quality, but the bonds do not last more than 3 weeks. I have followed all care instructions and use quality products to care for my extensions. I am an experienced extension user. I have gone back to my original more expensive brand as they last 3-4 months with proper care. I cannot in good conscience leave the 5 star rating I was coerced into providing. The product does not deserve it. The practice of making one change their rating to get replacements is shady and misguiding. Yes, I got a replacement pack, but it was of the same poor quality as my initial order. Shame shame.

title: Hard pressed, don’t pick much up, not very pigmented. Wish they provided more photos to choose color
text:
This claims to be titanium dioxide free, gluten free, made with natural and organic ingredients, vegan, and free of parabens, nano-particles, bismuth oxychloride, talc, silicones, mineral oil, GMOs, artificial fragrance, artificial preservatives, FD&C dyes, carmine, and phthalates. It is made in the USA. The ingredient list is on the product box and it is really short (see photos). It claims to be formulated with natural ingredients, such as Kaolin Clay and Jojoba Oil. They say they are cruelty free. The product page has a photo that says “Leaping Bunny Certified,” but the logo on the box is a PETA logo. I checked both websites and HYNT Beauty is certified by both Leaping Bunny and PETA.

I got the shade “Linen Kiss.” A little searching online showed it was a matte ivory. I really didn’t like they didn’t have much info at all about the shades to choose from. There weren’t any descriptions of the different shades to say whether they were matte, shimmer, etc. There weren’t photos other than the product in the little singles compact. I would have liked to have seen more product photos, like swatches comparing the different shades to help me choose, or at least a description of each shade. I had to search on Google and even when I went to their website there were only 4 shade options there. At least there they had a description for the 4 shades, but they only had the single photo of each in the singles compact. For a single eyeshadow coating $22, I expect more. The focus on the ingredients and what isn’t included is good, but they should also put a little attention on providing customers with more photos so they can easily pick a shade that’s right for them and be happy when the get it. Not have to guess what finish it has or if they shade is going to look like it does in the pan when they get it.

This comes in a little ziplock bag. Inside is a little outer product box.

It comes in a plastic singles compact. The top flips open easily.

It’s a matte ivory.

I show a photo where I swatched it. I did a finger swatch on my clean forearm (no lotion, primer, etc.). I swirled my finger in the pan and it seemed really hard pressed, like I wasn’t picking up much. I looked at my finger to see what I had picked up and should have been surprised after how much I swirled it in the pan that I didn’t have more, but I wasn’t really because of how hard pressed it felt. I took a photo showing it on my finger. As you can see, it isn’t very opaque and doesn’t look like I picked much up. I swirled a lot and that’s all I got. I swiped that onto my forearm. Then I went back into the pan. This time I pressed harder into the pan while I swirled. I picked up the same amount and put a second layer over the first one I had already done. Then, I did the same thing and did a different swipe. I did 3 layers for that one to show how it built up. It showed up enough on my fair skin, but I wasn’t a fan with how hard pressed this was. Maybe if I didn’t get such a light shade I’d like it more? But, I feel like the formula just isn’t too great and wouldn’t have great pigmentation with any color.

It’s nice and smooth.

Overall, its okay. It’s not for me. For me to spend $22 for a single eyeshadow, the eyeshadow needs to be pretty darn good. This just isn’t it. It’s too hard pressed for my liking. You don’t pick up much product and even when you do it doesn’t have that much pigmentation. Like I said, maybe with a different color it would be different, but I don’t think so. There’s way better options out there. I don’t recommend this.

title: Will not operate correctly on 120V
text:
Have an older Norelco 550TL which is a much better shaver than this new one. Had replaced the cutters perhaps 7 years ago, after obtaining the difficult to find replacements; that old shaver with the now old blades, is still a magnitude better than this new shaver. The new model runs very slow, so I assumed it was due to also being directly operable at 220volt. However my old 550TL operates at 220v as well, but still runs at nearly twice the speed of the new one. The 6423LC does hug the contour of the face better and is quieter, but the shave quality is quite poor. Requires covering the same area time after time after time...again and again. If would not have purchased this shaver if I could have found the correct replacement blades again.

Finally realized what is going on. This shaver is designed to run from the lowest noted to the highest noted voltage, only because it will operate on 220 maximum. What do I mean? The motor runs less than half speed at the lowest voltage and full speed at 220v, thus the shaving head is proportionally as slow also at 120 volts, thus requiring twice the time to shave. It should be fine at 220v, so if I even get to Europe, I am set. Otherwise I am screwed. Buy it if you want, but you have been told. Had I been able to return, I would have, but they say no return. I chalk this up as a win for Amazon (they got my money) but shame on them for knowingly offering a definitely mis-represented product....this is not like them at all.

FYI- I’ve tried at least 25 types of hair extensions, ponytails, hair scrunches, wigs, needed due to the evil side effect post Covid hair loss, so I thought I’d try these things out. This product has failed in so many ways. This is not what I expected and I would not recommend it.

title: Is there really a blade in this thing?
text:
I'm sixty-four and have been using Norelco shavers all of my adult life. When I needed a new one, my wife wanted to get it for my birthday. I specified a Norelco Arcitec, mostly because its looks made it look light and handy, and I anticipated that I would get my usual Norelco shave.

Was I ever wrong. From day one, I had to check to be sure there were blades in this thing. It's like a kid's toy shaver--it buzzes and runs around over the stubble, but gets very little of it after several passes. I kid you not, I can go over the same spot 6-8 times and then test it with my finger tips and not notice any change. I generally shave during a one-hour commute. With the Arcitec, it takes me a half-hour to get the job done--and poorly. The Arcitec has a tiny capacity to hold shavings and when it fills up (half way through one shave) it shaves even worse. If I skip shaving for even one day, the Arcitec is essentially useless against my two-day stubble.

I have a really OLD Norelco Speedshaver that I bought at an estate sale as a backup. This thing was old when I bought it twenty years ago. The previous owner used it to shave her legs. It's a model number SC7830. It looks like a style from the 1940s or early 1950s. It doesn't even have an on-off switch. I have no idea how old the blades are in this thing but it shaves circles around my Arcitec. I now use it instead of my Arcitec, which I threw away. (And my wife complains that I never throw away anything.)

Edit: I just came back and read a couple of glowing reviews of this Norelco Arcitec shaver. One of them accused reviewers like me of being employed by the competition. Well, I'm not. Like I said, I've used Norelco shavers for 40+ years, and I most likely will again. After my experiences with this model, I think those who claim to love it must work for Norelco--or they have peach-fuzz for whiskers, maybe. I have to wonder if the Arcitec was designed by a Norelco employee who was about to quit and go to work for a Norelco competitor. This Norelco Arcitec was just a complete waste of money. I'm still using my backup Norelco Speedshaver from the 1940s or 1950s. It shaves. Maybe if you're very young and still have peach-fuzz whiskers, the Arcitec would work for you, I wouldn't know.

title: Went for the full experience - went home disappointed
text:
I ordered the full line of the OZ Naturals products, I have normal to oily combination skin and here are the results after 30 days:

** Vitamin C Serum - No difference. It was so thin and runny, I'm not sure it did anything for my skin. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Facial Mask - This was supposed to be hydrating, but I found that it dried my face out terribly. I couldn't keep it on for the minimum time suggested because my face started to hurt from the drying feeling. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Scrub For Your Face - This was OK, but a little drying. I expected that since it's a scrub. Will keep this product and use every once and awhile.

** Facial Cleanser (orange bottle) - OMG this was SO drying! Yes, it does make the face smooth, but when you combine this with the toner and the moisturizer, it looked like I was in the sun all day because my face was bright red. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Facial Toner - The bottle says to use this after the shower to "lock in moisture". I didn't feel like my skin was any more moisturized. In fact, it didn't feel like anything. If I used this alone or with a "non-OZ" moisturizer, I was OK. If combined with 2 other products, it was like the trinity of hell for my face. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Facial Moisturizer (blue one with sea kelp) - Yea...went on smooth, but then my face felt "stiff" after it absorbed the moisturizer. After the sunburn experience, I tried again with just the face wash/moisturizer combo and I needed an additional moisturizer, so my face didn't feel like it was going to "crack". Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

Combining the face wash, toner, and moisturizer -
This got me twice - once I thought maybe I did something wrong and it took after sun aloe to make my face stop burning. The 2nd time I cursed my stupidity at trying again and will not use that combination (or the products because they will be going in the trash) again. I tried several different combinations of these products and was always met with 1 of 2 results - the fiery depths of hell on my face or feeling like my face was so dry I was standing in full sun in the desert. Neither was a pleasant experience for me.

I know some people like these products and I was hoping they would work for me, so I could get away from the products on the market that are polluted with chemicals, but this was a terrible experience for me. Back to the drawing board!

title: Rusted within 48 hours
text:
I used the small, black five star g-whiz twice in 48 hours. I rinsed the blades off with tap water. Next morning, the blades had rust on them. I got a full refund by Amazon since I bought it directly from them. End of story.

Wahl customer support, I want to buy and like your products, but now I've got to ask which of your products do not have this problem. I just want a cordless battery powered trimmer that won't rust. As sales and business owners, it really doesn't make economic sense to sell something with metal in it guaranteed to rust as soon as it hits water, since people are going to do a 180 and get a refund.

Maybe the metal does have the benefit of being easier to machine and result in higher quality blades, but it's really not an option to have easily oxidized metal in a product that gets washed frequently.

I'm open to buying Wahl trimmers again, but I need recommendations for which models won't have fundamental engineering design flaws. I'll spend the money, just tell me what actually works.

P.S. the trimmer works fine otherwise. Maybe a little wimpy in terms of power output, but no hair pulling. Pretty noisy, but who cares. Just lubricate it properly. It's smaller than the Remington MB4900, but the blade width is almost as long. It's lightweight and very small, so I guess if you have gigantic man-hands it might not offer the best ergonomics. I actually prefer non-permanent batteries, so that was a plus for me. The trimmer heads aren't easily removable for cleaning. I don't think the body is very waterproof (aside from the obvious aforementioned blade rusting), so be wary about using it in the shower.

text:

Taking the nozzle off and soaking it in hot water, then in 91% alcohol, didn’t do the trick, nor did switching nozzles between cans. I threw the whole thing away and started on the second can, which is developing the same problem though not quite as quickly. I may actually get a couple more weeks of use out of it before tossing it, too. Who knows what the third can will behave like, but I can guess. I’m long past the 30 day return window, so will just have to chalk this up to experience. A poor one.

Another reviewer noted on the back of her can it stated Not for Sale in the US. My can states Not for Sale in the EU which I assume is because of the fluorocarbon content. I wish I could find an environmentally friendly hairspray that would hold as well as this stuff.

title: Philips Norelco Arcitec 1060
text:
I have used Norelco shavers for 40+ years, and I love the look and weight of this shaver.

I used it for 6 months and was so dissatisfied I finally switched to the Braun Pulsonic.

The Arcitec shaves poorly and harshly. The famous floating heads are gone, instead the heads pivot from the center of the assembly - i.e. they tilt away from your skin rather than into your skin. You end up trying to shave with the middle of the shaver assembly, where there is no cutting head.

Also, they moved the trimmer inboard so it is hidden by your hand if you hold it the way you would normally. This you can adjust to.

They need a major redesign of the detachable shaving head assembly. If they made the cutting heads pivot on their centers instead of from the inside edge, it would probably work and they could sell guys like me the redesigned shaving head assembly. Maybe they could also go back to the Spectra cutters?

title: Form but not function -- take a pass on this razor.
text:
Be wary of this razor. It's a definite downgrade from previous Norelco razors in terms of function.

Pros:
- Looks cool
- Cleans easily
- Shaves stubble (and only stubble) close
- Can be returned to Norelco within 60 days for a full refund

Cons:
- Does not handle anything over stubble well for long. Has very shallow reservoirs for the hair to collect in and when you shave anything longer than stubble it gets gunked up and doesn't perform as well.
- Will spray hair everywhere if you tilt it off your face while running. This is a result of the shallow reservoirs. The hair seems to collect on top of the razor instead of inside it.
- Needs to be cleaned after each use. Hope you get all those stray hairs the first time!
- Head will shoot off and bounce around the room if you're not careful when drying it.
- Only has 65 minutes of shave time (compared to 85-120 on old models). It took about 10-15 mins per shave so I got 6 shaves in at best.
- Trimmer does not extend. It's pretty much impossible to see what you're trimming.

If you want a razor to shave stubble close and look cool then this is for you. Otherwise be prepared to stick the razor in it's coffin like carrying case and ship it back to Norelco.

Myself, I returned this and downgraded to the Norelco 9195XL (last year's model basically). It has none of the cons of the arcitec and it's 100 bucks cheaper new on ebay ... too bad amazon doesn't seem to carry it.

title: worst shaving experience
text:
This was my first rotory razor I purchased. I thought I would try something new, and the Philips name has always been good. I would have thought that a high name would have a better product and I figured that rotory razors should have come along way in the past 10 years. I have always used foil razors for years prior to this.
I used the razor for a week; trying different preshave chemicals to help reduce the burn I was receiving. The razor felt smooth to the skin, but it left my neck red and burning feeling all day long. Nothing helped to reduce that feeling either.
The only positive attribute is that Philips has the money back guarantee. There wasn't a catch at all, but it does take 4-6 weeks to receive the refund.
Needless to say, I went back to a foil razor, which happens to be a Panasonic Vortex. It is what I left to buy this Philips razor. I was never so happy to get rid of something. The Panasonic takes me half the time to shave, gives me a closer shave, and no burn. All of the razors already positive features where enhanced when I continued using the remaining Electric Shave preshave prior to shaving with the Panasonic.
I will never purchase another rotory razor again! It was the worst shaving experience I have had with razors.

title: Disappointing!
text:
I read with interest, the most favorable review for this shaver. This person mentioned that this is their first electric shaver after a lifetime of using blades. I guess if that is the case, the reviewer doesn't have much to compare this product with. Having had previous Norelco models as well as a Remington and a couple Brauns... I have a bit more actual experience with competing products.

A few years back, we bought a second home. We decided to stock our vacation home with everything needed so that we would not have to carry luggage and we could just head to an airport and go. I had used Norelco shavers for a number of years. About 10 years ago, my wife bought me a Braun 7 series shaver. What a difference. It gave me a much smoother and closer shave with less chafing and discomfort. I wasn't and still am not impressed with the so-called cleaning system that Bruan has designed. But the shaver itself was terrific. About 2 years ago, the battery in my beloved Braun started to fail. So I bought a new 790CC Braun Shaver. This one was even better than the first. So as we gathered things to take to our second home, I asked my wife to pick up another Braun shaver. The 790CC is not an inexpensive product. So my thrifty wife, knowing I had used Norelcos in the past, picked up the Arcitec shaver on sale.

What a disappointment! To be honest, I can't find anything that is a distinct positive about this product. Let me organize my thoughts just a bit...

1. Size - The shaver head is just too big. It is hard to maneuver in tight areas such as at the upper lip and nose. Requires using the trimmer to get acceptably close.
2. Performance - I do not have a heavy beard. I find that 24 hours of growth is the limit for this shaver. If your facial hair is allowed to grow for any longer than that, the shaver will not cut it. If you have a heavy beard, this shaver simply wont do the job.
3. Cleaning - The heads clog very quickly. Once they do, the shaver will not cut at all. The Braun by comparison, can usually go a week before cleaning.
4. Trimmer - As others have said... Small and in an awkward position. It's foolish to suggest that the shaver head should be removed to facilitate trimming. Better to suggest that the Phillips/Norelco engineers should take a crack at a better design.

I have used this shaver intermittently for the last two years. My older Norelcos were far better than this one. So that being said, I finally decided enough is enough and ordered another Braun from Amazon.

title: If you sleep alone
text:
The marketing blurb says, among other things "this advanced man face care formula features stem cells to help revive the skin and smooth out imperfections".
Well... stem cells, if they were actually somehow harvested, in a cosmetics container, mixed with various other chemicals and ingredients would necessarily be dead and therefore completely irrelevant. And, of course, the stem cells would help address things such as diabetes and repair of heart muscle following heart attack, not zits on one's face. Not to mention that they would need to be live and 'human' cells. So, I am quite confident that the 'stem cells' claim is untrue and, even if it were true, the presence of dead stem cells in a cream would make zero difference.
Other than that, the cream is thick and, as other reviewer found, it has an aggressive smell that reminded me of Noxzema. So I would never use it during the day. At night, it would probably be Okay if used by men who sleep alone.

title: THE DESCRIPTION OF THIS WIG IS A COMPLETE LIE!!!
text:
I just want to start by saying that I have been ordering wigs from Amazon for about 5 years and I have NEVER been more disappointed in a wig in all of this time! The wig that I received is NOTHING like the wig that is advertised! Everything from the cap construction to the length of the hair itself was completely different. The first thing it says in the description is "13X6", but my wig has a 4X6 14" closure. I have very limited parting space and the top is so much shorter than the rest of the wig. I ordered 22 inches, the wig arrived about 18-20 inches and shrank to 16 inches when curled. the ends of the hair are incredibly thin. Another feature listed in the description is "Transparent Lace Pre Plucked". I received ashy beige lace that I then had to tint because it did not blend with my skin the way actual transparent lace does. also the 14 inch 4x6 closure was slightly plucked but rest of the hairline was blunt and untouched. I'm positive that even if the creator of this wig wanted to pluck the rest of the hairline, they could not because there are tracks location close to the hairline where lace would typically be on an actual 13x6 wig. I had to cut layers in order to blend the short closure in with the rest of the hair. I have no idea where they found the pictures that they use for this wig because it is nothing like what you see pictured. I have never been more disappointed in a human hair wig that I have ordered from Amazon!

I will be updating this review with pictures of everything that I have described.

title: They recommend to use it in the morning on DRY skin
text:
I bought this serum from ScienceSerum directly and returned it after 3 weeks of use since it dried out my around eye area beyond repair. Skin in the corners of my eyes started to crape, lines and wrinkles became more deep and pronounced because of the dryness, puffiness and dark circles appeared. It has been 4 weeks since I stopped using it, but I still have been able neither to quench the dryness nor diminish puffiness no matter what I do. I went to my derm, he said I have severe allergic reaction and prescribed steroids to combat the symptoms.

At the time when skin care layering is paramount, this product is a huge logistical failure.
It is very difficult to incorporate the serum into either- morning or night - routine. They recommend to use it in the morning on DRY skin, which means you would need to cleanse your face, wait for it to dry, apply it, then wait again for the serum to dry. Who has time for that much waiting in the morning? Another issue for me was that I could not leave my skin dry for that much time without applying toner and Vit C. But then, when the serum was dried, vitamin C would be washed off along with the serum. I wrote to the company and asked them how to properly layer it with other skincare products I use (Vitamin C, Retin-A, essences etc) they had no idea!
Another problem - it is extremely difficult to get it off your skin completely without pulling and tagging your delicate eye area. But if you do not pulling and tagging, the product stays on your skin and destroys it very rapidly.
If you have a question and write to Scienceserum, be prepared to contact them at least three times before they respond.
If you are going to buy directly from them and decide to return the serum, you will be responsible for return shipping AND they are going to withhold 20% of the serum cost for the original shipping. text: I bought this brush for 2 reasons. 1 to keep with me to brush beard throughout the day and to be able to put beard balm on without using my hands, this product fails at both. The main problem with this brush is how ridiculously soft the bristles are. I've had 3 or 4 different boars hair brushes (non designer or expensive) since I grew a manly beard couple years ago and they've all been alittle different stiffness but none have been anywhere near this soft and useless on a beard especially if it has more then 4 weeks of growth. title: Not what is pictured -- false advertising.
text:
Not sure if there are differences in wig standards with these reviews or if we're all reviewing different wigs but the wig I purchased (20 inch, 360 lace, dark brown color, human hair) is not much like the wig that is pictured. I think the only thing they got right was the length. The description on the wig notes that it is indeed the wig I bought but the pictures on Amazon that showcase the wig are false advertising.

In short -- THE BAD:
- LACE: Lace is MUCH darker than what is pictured -- when you put it on, it looks like a hair hat. Not many of us have a scalp that dark.
- PART: There is NO part (middle, side, etc). Are we supposed to do this part ourselves? If so -- make a note of it.
- THICKNESS: The wig is about 6x thicker than what is pictured so it looks fake. It's super heavy and if you put it up in a ponytail, good luck finding a hair tie that can go around it at least once.
- QUALITY: I think it's a mixture of real and synthetic hairs. Upon closer inspection the hair type varies. I did spot quite a few split ends but the thickness of each hair strand isn't consistent which tells me they mixed fibers.
- LACE INTEGRITY: The lace curls up so be prepared to glue it down in case you plan on not returning this wig. I don't think it can be worn glue-less.
- KNOTS: They say they bleached the knots... but they didn't. The front part literally looks like connect the dots on graph paper.
- COLOR: Wig is a mixture of black and dark brown hairs... def. not just dark brown. So, it's much darker than you'd expect it to be per the photos and the description.
- WIG CAP SIZE: I own about 20 wigs. This is the only one that swam on my head (I have a medium sized head). The cap is way too large for me and using the bands will make the outer cap edges curl.
- SCALP CAP: Wearing a cap underneath (black or beige) will show. You can literally see the outline of where it ends on your scalp which is interesting since the lace is so dark.
- CURL: To test if it can curl, I tried it with both a curling iron and natural curlers. Nothing happened (which is further proof to me that they mixed synthetic fibers within the wig).

The Good:
- The baby hairs look decent (although the super visible knots take away from the job they did here).

Maybe if you take it to a salon to get it treated (fade color of lace, bleach the knots, thin the wig out, color correct, high-end band sewing) -- you might make it work. BUT -- how much will that run you up for? I don't think this wig is worth $25... much less the $180 currently advertised. FAKE!

Will upload photos soon.

title: More silicone than argan oil. Actual ingredients not clearly listed.
text:
I bought this because the seller listed the main ingredients as argan oil and resvesterol, when in fact the product is full of silicon and demethicone is listed before argan oil. I can see why there are rave reviews from other users. This will give your hair a great TEMPORARY shine and silky soft feel but will end up robbing it of shine shortly and prevent your hair from absorbing moisture. You are not coating your hair with Arian oil but a rubber derivative. So th cuticle lays down short term but never gets the moisture that is causing the damage and frizz to begin with. I think someone who has science in their name would know that. Long term demethicone use will cause more drying and damage and is not good for your hair.

I had actually wanted to use this product on my face, not hair because of the resvesterol. But it has an extremely strong scent of sandalwood that is overpowering and I would never be able to use it on my face.

The bottle arrived in a box but leaked all over. I would have returned anyway because of the demethicone and smell. I bought pure cold pressed argan oil to use instead. It smells naturally like poo as all of them do but the smell dissipates in a few minutes.

I do think the seller should make its ingredients clear to prospective buyers and not just list the deceptive "main ingredients" omitting the ingredients that are listed first when the package actually arrives and therefore are really the main ingredients.

title: Engineered to fail
text:
This product is good while it lasts; it'll clean your teeth better than almost anything out there (unless you have tartar, then you'll need something with a bit more power) and stimulate your gums. However, having autopsied this model, I am convinced that it was engineered to fail under typical conditions after a time, perhaps to motivate the purchase of a more expensive model, which will itself become useless when the irreplaceable batteries go out.

The first one I bought lasted a year, and even that long only after I learned that you have to plug the two holes in the back of the battery compartment to prevent the corrosion from taking place. By the end, batteries were lasting one week tops, at 2x use per day. I also learned that you have to hit it against hard objects when it won't turn on and sometimes then it'll go. You also need to scrape off any rust from the battery contacts occasionally.

Knowing these quirks, I bought another one and immediately plugged up the holes in the back and put tape around the battery cap. However, it has now lasted only a month. There's no rust or corrosion to speak of, however, it just doesn't turn on anymore.

Today I autopsied the first sonicare to see why it had failed (the new one is still on warranty). In taking it apart, it's clear that most of your money goes into buying a tank-like shell around the $1 worth of electronics. This would be a good thing, if there were not two gaping holes in the battery cap that let water in anyway and the shoddy rubber seal. After taking it apart, it's clear why the corrosion so quickly leads the failure. They protect everything on the circuit-board from corrosion by putting glue over it, except the battery contacts, and the contacts and wires that lead to the solenoid coil (that makes the brush vibrate). The contacts that lead to the solenoid and the battery contacts are also strategically located next to each other on the circuit board, so they can corrode together quickly using any moisture from the adjacent battery-terminal holes, while the non-essentials like the timer are located on the other side of the board and completely sealed off from the ambient air by glue. This also explains why hitting it sometimes allows it to start; you're shaking some of the corrosion loose.

The switch is also of questionable design, being nothing more than a paper-thin piece of plastic with some kind ring on it that's slightly more conductive than the plastic.

If the replacement that I get out of the warranty fails, I think I'll try a cybersonic or an oral-b; hopefully their teams of engineers weren't paid to make something less reliable than a politician.

Why can't they make a sonic toothbrush with no batteries, that plugs into the wall, and lasts a lifetime? Or just quit making these to fail so readily?

title: Fleeing back to a real razor
text:
For two decades I have fought an uphill battle with a downhill class of products, and I'm throwing in the towel. I've abandoned this electric razor and gone back to a real razor (a basic Gillette Mach 3).

I switched to a multi-headed electric razor over 20 years ago. "Stick with it for 30 days" the instructions implored. Yes, it got better, but never equalled my old 2-blade razor. The convenience suckered me in, and the habit was set. I meticulously cleaned and maintained my electric razors, but never attained a clean shave.

But I stuck with it. Replaced the heads, and that worked for a while, but then same old same old. New electric razors seem to get worse. A little Phillips Philishave 30 worked pretty well (2 heads, *battery* powered), but not great.

When this Arcitec came on board, I said "this is it!" Pricey, but there can be no better, right? Of all the electric razors I have used, I must say that this is the worst. The cleaning system works to a point, but there are inevitably hairs that get lodged in the razor head. And the razor head is effectively *NOT CLEANABLE* except by painstaking surgery to extract lodged hairs.

And the shave? OK, this is not a scientific double-blinded study, but I do honestly believe that this razor provided me with the worst shave of all electric razors I have owned. It got me to jump ship and try a middle-of-the-road Gillette Mach 3. The result ...

HEAVEN! Blades have gotten SO much better since 20 years ago. Super clean shave, no nics, no problems, no irritation ... why did I wait so long??

title: Poor craftsmanship, and Velcro catches in hair.
text:
They use Velcro, the old type, that has a soft side (not a problem) and a rough side - which catches on *everything* especially ones hair (proper “application or not).
Also that same Velcro is sewn on/attached so poorly, that I had to reinforce their dismally lacking stitching.
Fine, it does fit nicely, and the actual material that it’s made of it pleasant and absorbent in all the right ways, and it stays in place.

BUT THERE’S NO EXCUSE FOR THE MISERY THAT THE VELCRO THEY USE (and its poor attachment) CAUSES.

Especially when there are so many new(er) Velcro-type technologies out there - one of my favorite types being where both sides are essentially the “soft/smooth) side.
If it works for my cable organization wraps, I don’t see why it wouldn’t here.
Would spare my hair (and the cable organization “Velcro” wraps, work just fine wet - consider me curious; and if I were more inclined towards arts & crafts, or had the time, maybe I would sacrifice one of my cable organization “adhesive” wraps and use them instead of this lovely example of 1980s cutting-edge tech.)

title: This products contains the toxic chemicals methylene chloride and methanol.
text: There has been much discussion about this product on Amazon and professional nail tech blogs.  One of the most serious issues is the absence of a safety data sheet (SDS) from the manufacturer.  By law, manufacturers selling chemical products in the United States must provide accurately documented SDS upon request.  The manufacturer of this product has not provided such a SDS.  We ordered a product through Amazon which arrived via China Post/USPS identified as 'Makeup Tools' for customs purposes.  As professional chemists, we analyzed this product (pH, FTIR, TGA, elemental analysis and GC-MS).  This alkaline product contains methylene chloride, methanol, n-butoxyethanol, a series of n-alkane hydrocarbons and two different petroleum boiling point distillate fractions.  Methylene chloride and methanol are known toxic chemicals which can be absorbed through the skin and inhaled into your respiratory tract.  Please use Google to search for and open the SDS docs for these two chemicals and read the hazards.  This product is similar to a methylene chloride containing industrial paint strippers which are being removed from the marketplace due to their toxic ingredient(s).  This product is not suitable for sale to the general public or to the professional nail community as a nail polish remover.  AMAZON is derelict in its duty to police the products it sells; in this case the product is highlighted as "Amazon's Choice".  Please be aware that there are other brands of 'Magic Remover' being offered for sale with a similar name, paper label and bottle shape.  Buyer Beware!

title: THE. WORST.
text:
AWFUL. I was really hoping this mascara would fill the sad, gaping hole left by the discontinuance of Scandal Queen, which was the most perfect, amazing mascara EVER, but nope, the Quattro Film Type mascara is a hugely over-priced disaster.

FIRST: The design sucks. The piece in the tube that's supposed to scrape off excess mascara doesn't work well, so the brush pulls out too much mascara with random blobs of it in places. Then, the brush bristles are waayyy too short, especially for such thick mascara with fibers, so the bristles can't properly pull through your lashes to distribute the mascara and the mascara just kinda blobs on. I included some photos below to try to show the blobs and how short the bristles are, but I'm not sure if you can tell (black mascara on black bristles is hard to photograph). Where there aren't blobs on the brush, the mascara lightly coats the corresponding lashes, resulting in a very uneven, lumpy/chunky application. And you can't even use the brush to try to distribute the mascara through your lashes evenly because there's still too much mascara on it due to the crappy scraper-thing, so if you try to do that, it just globs on more mascara and now you're starting to look like a toddler's puffy paint art project.

SECOND: Usually you can even out even the clumpiest mascaras using an eyelash comb after the mascara dries a bit. But not with Quattro because combing it actually pulls off large chunks of the mascara (I think because it's so clumpy/chunky on application, it all sticks together and comes off in pieces). So the length gets all uneven because the fibers lengthen your lashes, but the combing pulls off some of these fibers. And the volume becomes patchy and there are literally gaps in the mascara. There have been a few times where it looked like I had a floating eyelash because black mascara covered half the eyelash, then there was a gap of light-colored natural lash without mascara, and then the mascara continued at the tip of my eyelash. I've never had anything like this happen with mascara.

THIRD: I don't know this for sure, but I swear my eyelashes got shorter and thinner because of this mascara. They were very long and thick because I've used GrandeLash and LiLash for a long time, but a couple months after using this Quattro mascara I realized my lashes were noticeably thinner and shorter, even though I was still using LiLash. I was still using this mascara even though I didn't like it because it's SO expensive, but I stopped using it when I realized my lashes looked thinner/shorter. It's only been a couple weeks since I stopped using it so it's too soon to know for sure if it's the mascara.

I'm 33 y/o and I've tried A LOT of mascaras, and this is the worst mascara I've EVER used. Most of the mascaras I haven't liked are because they smudge too easily or don't add enough length or volume, but those problems are fixable by adding a second mascara and/or layering. But this mascara is in a class by itself--it's not fixable, causes a mess, and possibly hurts your eyelashes. I don't usually have such strong feelings about a product, but this mascara is THE WORST.

title: I really wanted to love it...
text: I'm a huge fan of sandalwood and have used Mysore Sandalwood bar soap from this company many times in the past.  I had to quit using the bar soap because of its drying effect on my skin.  When I saw this body wash in the same scent, I thought I'd give it a try.  I was a little put off by the price, but I reasoned that luxury body washes do sell for that much, so it's reasonable to sell an imported specialty body wash for a similar price.  When I received my body wash from Amazon, I eagerly opened the package and used it the next time I showered.  The first thing I initially smelled was the sandalwood fragrance that I'm accustomed to.  Then it hit me: MOTH BALLS!  Intermingled with the beautiful sandalwood scent is the offensive smell of moth balls.  I'm not sure why or how, but it's there.  I've used the body wash a few times to be sure and every time I smell it.  Now, when I'm done showering, the fragrance that lingers on my skin is only that of the familiar sandalwood soap.  Unfortunately, I won't be purchasing this body wash again, since I don't like smelling the moth ball scent while I shower.

- First thing is trying to squeeze to open - the outside rubber is highly oiled, loose, and therefore just rotates around and one can't grip on the clip to open. I tried to stabilize with my other hand and the inside clip just rotates away instead of opening even with 2 hands. Almost impossible to open! I am not clumsy or incompetent and tout myself as pretty handy and capable yet these things are flawed right from the start. I wrestle with just trying to use a simple alligator clip and it floors me that the main purpose of these do not work right.
- Some of the clips just don't close properly. The springs are cheap and so forget clipping on a fine wire like a resistor with the ones that won't close properly. I use the flawed ones that don't close all the way on a larger item like my multimeter leads. See photo
- None of these are soldered like many other reviews state. They are crimped. See photo
- The jaws are rough cut and work fine (when you finally get them opened) for larger items but for smaller and very thin items (think resistors) they are not what you want. See photo where I had to bend the resistor wire to get it to stay in the jaws.

While these are inexpensive and fine for the non-discerning use they are by no means competent and have serious flaws that prevent one from using these on many fine and detailed projects. Since there are so many 5 star reviews I can only think the use case would be not for electronics projects and perhaps a set once and forget use?!?

title: Perfect Placing Stamper! (updated)
text:
The clear stamper came just as described. I haven't actually used it on my nails yet but I have played around with it on some paper and it picks up the images perfectly. After reading some concerning reviews on other clear stampers I was hesitant to purchase this one. However, I have had no problems as of yet. The only flaw is that there are two little dent/scratches on the stamper head and I am afraid eventually it will lead to bigger dents/scratches. With it being so inexpensive I wouldn't mind purchasing another one for back-up, just in case. I do not use any scrapers that come with the stampers, as I use gift cards because they are much easier to use and swipe with.

The stamper head is squishy but not marshmallow squishy. It is possible to squish on your nail without rolling, so long as you do not have extremely wide nail beds. It is a little hard to get used to being able to see through and it takes some practice getting it lined up exactly where you want, but it's easier once you do it a few times. As I stated earlier, the images are very crisp and clean when being picked up. Instead of squishing down like I did with my other stamper I instead try to roll/flick the stamper across. This is more for the fear of damaging the stamper, as I've read about others who did not have success with clear stampers.

Make sure that when you use it you do not clean it with acetone/polish remover as it will eventually make the stamper head cloudy and no longer see through. Also, do not buff or anything before first use, I found that it picks up perfectly without having to do any of that.

I highly recommend getting this stamper if you love to stamp but have problems with perfect placing, such as myself.

*****UPDATE******

I have no idea what happened but I've recently been trying to use this stamper and it will just not work. I've used so many different polishes, different brands and nothing! I had no problem at all and picked up images very well, however now it picks up less than half of the image which is extremely frustrating. I spent about 2 hours this morning doing all kinds of different things, using different polishes, using different techniques, different stamping plates and nothing is working! I've tried priming it like you would a non-clear stamper which includes wiping the head with acetone and buffing it with a file.

For quite a while, I just used two old margarine tubs to soak my denture. (Pro tip: soak your denture in plain water in a separate container and then rinse it thoroughly before putting it in the cleaning solution, and then your cleaning solution won't get nasty.) But when the lids of my margarine tubs started to crack, I decided to get some "real" denture cups. Yeah...I should have just eaten some more margarine and washed out a new tub.

These cups are not in the least impressive. The lid of the blue cup snaps shut but isn't remotely leakproof--tip it just slightly and you'll have water or cleaning solution sloshing all over. The lid of the white cup doesn't even snap shut. It just barely rests on top of the cup and strainer, and if you don't watch what you're doing when you pick up the container, you'll find yourself holding the lid and looking at the cup and water/solution all over the floor. Furthermore, the two cups are far too hard to stack. The white one can't go on top of the blue one because the lid of the blue one is curved, but putting the blue one on top of the white one is precarious because the blue one is wider. And I find it surprisingly annoying to have two containers that won't stack taking up twice as much space as necessary in my tiny bathroom. About the only feature of these cups that is at all handy is the little strainer thing, and since my denture is plastic and floats, I don't find even that feature very useful.

Bottom line: you can soak dentures in pretty much any container, and you can find two small plastic containers with flat tops and secure lids for considerably less than the cost of these. Toast with margarine, anyone?

Kava kava is awesome, but there's some sketchy things that occur in the kava realm. One of which is using other parts of the Piper Methysticum (Kava) plant or using a different species altogether. This can be dangerous, and very taxing on the liver. It'll get you krunk, sure, but at what cost?
Kava is one of those things that you should do your research and spend an extra few bucks to get the good, real stuff. title: Cloyingly sweet non-pineapple fragrance, and the quality of the products felt cheap.
text:
I really wanted to like this product, and I love pineapple, so I was super excited when it arrived. Unfortunately, I was let down by the quality of the actual products. They make a cute gift set, but that's really all they have going for them.

I love the smell of pineapple, but I found the scent of these products to be unpleasant. They smell very cloyingly sweet and artificial, and not much like pineapple at all. The whipped body soap had a nice texture, but it left my skin dry, and it took a lot of product just to get clean. The body butter felt sticky and greasy, and not all that luxurious. My skin was left a bit tacky, and not very moisturized even after it was absorbed. The bath soak is alright, but it has the same unfortunate scent as the other products, and you really don't get much product, so it's more appropriate for foot soak than a bath. The body scrub was probably the best product out of the bunch, and it creates a nice lather when mixed with water. It left my skin soft, but unfortunately was also quite drying.

Overall, I can't recommend this product. The presentation of the product is adorable, and I love that it's vegan... but the quality of this skincare product set just isn't very good.

I started with the recommended heating time of 20 seconds. This made the mask too hot and I had to let it cool for a couple of minutes. So I incrementally started decreasing the heating time. I’m down to 15 seconds for it to be warm enough but not too hot to put on my eyes.

The recommended time for use is 10-20 minutes. It doesn’t retain heat to use for even 5 minutes. So I either get a mask that’s too hot to apply, or not hot enough to produce the therapy it’s recommended for.

What a waste of $25. I wouldn’t recommend this product to anyone and wish I could get my money back. In this economy, every dollar counts.

text:
I love this hairspray. It takes some getting used to....it goes on wet, sticky, and a bit crunchy, but don't worry...once it dries, it holds beautiful and is touch-ably soft with lots of hold. **update 6/29/18: I ordered a second bottle and it is disastrous. Not sure if the formula changed or what, but it now leaves my hair VERY sticky and a knotted mess! If there is any moisture or humidity in the air, it turns my hair crunchy, sticky and impossible to brush through with my fingers or a hairbrush. I am so disappointed. I had such high hopes and a positive experience with my first bottle, but not anymore! I will be switching to something else. I would now give this product 2 stars! It also gives a really nice CRISP line, which is what I want.

But it has parabens, which have been found in breast cancer tumors. The Cosmetic Ingredient Review & the FDA have found parabens to be safe but I don't really trust either (the CIR is sponsored BY the industry it reviews, hm). There's been no proven link and the study that found the parabens didn't study how much parabens are in normal tissue. So it's really up to you if you care about parabens in your products. title: Too creamy for eyes and cheeks, too dry/messy for lips
text:
I really wanted to love this; I've been trying to radically reduce my waste and simultaneously use more natural products, and this seemed like such a perfect fit. I didn't mind the small size at all; that was part of my goal.

Unfortunately, both the pink & red lip/cheek colors make my cheeks break out, and the pink is too drying and patchy on my lips (I'm over 35, so it's possible this will work better for younger skin). The red works nicely for lip coloring on initial application and isn't drying, but it bleeds badly after wearing it for any real length of time, and then you start to have fruit-punch mouth.

The lip balm at bottom may well be the worst part. It is simultaneously not moisturizing (feels like more of a gloss than a balm) and it half-melts in even the slightest warmth, so every time I touch it I get a giant gob of it.

The highlight and bronzer might work well for younger skin, but they are very glittery. For me, I would only use these on my eyes, where they slide around horribly (even with primer). They are gorgeous in color, but just not a good fit for me, and possibly not for anyone over 35.

text:
I held off reviewing the Plum Smooth Sweet Plum soft wax for a few months till I got used to it and I have to say I DON'T LIKE it one bit and won't buy it again.

I went to school for Aesthetics and I've been waxing myself and friends for at least 3 yrs now, this is the second wax I have bought and didn't like, sadly this is much more $$ then the other. I thought since it was a bit more $$ that it would be good, yeah not so. I've waxed my underarms a few times with this wax and each time I end up with painful underarms that are RED and painful, and it takes at least 3 days for this to go away, again I've waxed with a few other waxes and only a soy wax did I have an adverse reaction to.

The first time I used this wax I didn't have good results with it taking all the hair off, so I went over the area a second time with the wax, I realize you shouldn't go over the area a second time with wax but it wasn't catching the hair, I thought well that's why this happened, but I made sure NOT to do that again, but same thing happened and I did it again (hard to just toss wax that's $$) this time and it happened again, I did NOT reapply after the first application, but I used what was on the wax strip to try and pick up the left on the skin hair, I've done this with other waxes and NEVER has it left my under arms this way - that is non except a soy wax which I'll never touch again either.

If you don't mind the price, the try it maybe you'll have a different reaction/results then me, but I found this not the greatest at taking hold of the hair (underarms, legs, back and bikini area) - I tried on high heat and low heat and each time I didn't have good results using this wax, OH and I did one other's under arms and yeah, she had a similar reaction to the wax as I. I would say use with caution, everyone reacts differently, but if I don't like how it works on me then I won't use it on anyone else.... Still on the hunt for a wax I love...

There is inconsistency in the length of the individual lashes (some are the same length the entire strip of lashes, while other attempt to mimic the shorter lashes of the inner eye, with varying levels of success/failure). These are a little thin, a little longer than a human eye, and will generally not look right unless you are an expert at trimming&applying lashes and makeup, and you manage to find 2 that match so that your eyes look symmetrical.

text:
You can tell Intuit is feeling the pressure and knows they're losing relevance by the way they've put this together. Quickbooks itself is fine. It works. It does what quickbooks does (which is create headaches and break regularly, along with compromising your security and privacy if you don't lock it down). However, when you pay $250-300 for some software, the software is only a small part of the package.

Customer service and tech help are the two biggest parts of the package, and well.... They're just crap....

Making the payroll side of this a subscription system after charging an extra $100 is just greedy. Forget it. I can find open source payroll systems that're more secure, easier to use and free sans the donation I will make out of appreciation for work well done.

If you're going to charge a subscription, don't make me pay up front. If you want me to pay up front, don't charge a subscription. Under no circumstances will I tolerate double dipping from a software company.

Sadly I'm a bit too lazy to move all of my information over to another system just yet, so it looks like I'm stuck with QB's not-so-funny little quirks for another year.

title: Costume quality, don't buy for daily wear
text:
I received this wig for free to test and evaluate. I will say upfront that I am not a "person who wears this type of synthetic wigs all the time" so I can't judge the quality like someone who does. I can only judge based on my perceptions.

The wig shows up with a wig cap included. That is a bonus point in my eyes. There were instructions included for washing the wig. That is also a bonus.

The cut and style were not as expected. It is more frizzy looking and the bangs are very long, much longer they appear in the picture. There was really no way to make the bangs not hang halfway over my eyes. The overall cut of the wig is best described as "Cut by a toddler hyped on sugar, using a Flowbee." (Google it. Flowbee was a thing supposed to cut in layers, but many people learned it simply butchered your hair in quick fashion.) There is no rhyme or reason to these layers. Some are long, some are short, some are in between. None of them make a style. The odd mix of frizzy curls tossed in amongst this tragedy of layers is even more odd.

I know that I am missing the point and this style of hair do is in vogue somewhere, in some time frame. Perhaps on Paris runways where they have fanciful hair styles?

The wig arrives untangled, just requiring some finger combing, but after an hour of wear, it began to tangle. Most quality synthetic wigs give you more time than that. It wasn't even a hot day and I was not sweating or doing anything to tangle it. This is one of those "I want to look like I didn't comb my hair and am so cool that I just pulled a beanie cap on.", kind of wigs. Because a beanie cap might be the only way to wear this style and pull it off. The hair itself is made from a shiny synthetic, it is slightly too shiny. This coupled with the cut makes it appear there are split ends all over, until you get close enough to realize it is fake hair.

The seller really tried to make this a good sale for people by including the wig cap and washing directions. This wig has the makings of a good wig. The under side of the wig is slightly stretchy and is adjustable as I have found with my more expensive wigs. The style and the quality of the hair don't cut it. I also want to note that I am not sure what they mean by heat resistant, I would not suggest putting heat anywhere near this wig.

In closing, this is a costume quality wig, one designed for use 2-3 times before becoming hopelessly dread locked.

title: Ingredients don't match up
text:
As someone who suffers from chronic insomnia (and the lovely, inescapable dark raccoon circle eyes that come with it), I was pretty excited to try this. I’ve only used it for one day, and the gel is pleasant enough to use, but what I want to bring up is the disparity between the ingredients that are advertised for Nuju Revitalizing Eye Gel, and the actual ingredients. I’ll break this down the best I can.

Right off the bat I noticed that this product claims to be paraben free, but has a number of contradicting Ingredients: Ethylparaben, Butylparaben, Propylparaben, Isobutylparaben. This could be a major problem for anyone with allergies or sensitivities. This product also claims to have time released retinol, which is notably missing from the ingredient list. I’ve listed almost every ingredient in this eye cream, and its function, below. Personally I think this will be useful for moisturizing, and perhaps a temporary rejuvenated look, but it doesn’t seem to pack enough punch to tackle my under eye circles. Because of the disparity between advertised ingredients and the actual, I’m giving this two stars. Keep in mind I don’t claim to be a scientist. Just going off of easily available information.

Herbal Ingredients:
Cucumis Sativus (Cucumber) Extract (Skin Conditioner); Chamomilla Recutita (Matricaria) extract (thought to increase blood flow and aid in “congestion” under the skin); Camellia Sinesis Leaf Extract (Green Tea extract. Generally only high concentrations have substantial effects on skin, but thought to help reduce swelling and inflammation among other things)

Of Interest:
Ceramide 3 (part of naturally occurring skin structure, it helps retain moisture, regulates cellular barrier repair); Sphingolipids (naturally occurring in the body, it functions as protection for cells against environmental factors); Hesperidin Methyl Chalcone (naturally occurring bioflavinoid, often used for under eye circle treatments, helps combat free radical damage and inflammation); Dipeptide-2 (effective skin conditioner, believed to help improve lymphatic circulation and so often found in under eye cream to reduce dark circles); Palymitoyl Tetrapeptide-7 (helps reduce inflammation. Increases collagen production when paired with Palmitoyl-Oligopeptide, which is not listed as an ingredient for this product); Camellia Sinesis Leaf Extract (Green Tea extract. Generally only high concentrations have substantial effects on skin, but thought to help reduce swelling and inflammation among other things)

Everything else:
Cetearyl Ethylhexanoate (emollient and skin conditioner); Propylene Glycol (aids with shelf stability); Carbomer (thickener/controls gel consistency); Polysorbate 20 (emulsifier/solubilizer); Triethanolamine ( ph adjuster *a “moderate concern” level ingredient for potential toxicity*); Hydroxypropyl Methycellulose (used for sustained release of ingredients); Ethylhexyl (lubricant/makes skin look soft and smooth); Cocoate (derived from coconut oil, skin conditioner); Steareth-20 (surfactant and emulsifier, often found in eye cream); Butylene Glycol (solvent and used to make creams more easily spreadable); Phenoxyethanol (Chemical preservative); Titanium Dioxide CI 77891 (white pigment and sunscreen); Cyclomethicone, Dimethiconol, Phenyl Trimethicone (liquid silicone, creates a temporary skin plumpness)

title: Not just cotton and silk - contains polyester
text:
I won't say the product is necessarily bad, but I certainly do not like it and am not pleased with the disparity between the description and the actual product.

While the amazon page says these eye-covers are made of cotton and silk, the product packaging and tags both indicate the product is cotton, silk, AND polyester. I would not have bought these had I known this as my wife reacts to polyester. This just leaves me with another useless set of eye covers that my wife can't use.

Also, I personally find these uncomfortable. The silk is nothing like my nice soft silk shirts. It is still a shiny and smooth fabric, yet also an uncomfortably rough (I'm not sure how better to describe it -- it's like running your skin over tiny closely spaced wires), fabric that is very hot to wear on your face. Furthermore, I found that I got a headache both times I tried wearing these.

My wife has previously made some passable eye-covers out of cotton socks that we both can wear -- and I find significantly more comfortable. She's suggested that maybe she can try taking these apart and using the straps and cotton parts and making better cotton-sock eye-covers. I'm skeptical and am considering returning these. I'm certainly not happy.

If you like the really slick-abrasive feeling fabrics like cheap silks or cheap satins, and if you don't have any issue with the polyester in these, I can't really see a problem with them. They could probably benefit from being a bit larger, but they're 'pillowy'-enough (for lack of a better word) to block out most of the light and fill in the gaps around the edges. Mystery as to why they give me a headache, but they've enough good reviews that it can't be common.

I'm giving them 2 stars because I think the description is misleading and I don't like them, but also because I think a more moderate rating would get this lost among rating of people who are happy with the item. I always read some of the reviews and I wish I'd seen a review like this before purchasing.

Unfortunately I have to agree with some of the more critical reviews of this product. I say unfortunately, because the vacuum actually works pretty good when the unit is new. But ask those people who rave on and on about this unit how well their trimmer is working after a few months use and i bet you will get a totally different answer. The suction power substantially decreases after a few months of use it and it drops clumps of hair every where. And this is despite cleaning the unit thoroughly after each use.

There are just too many other problems with this trimmer to recommend it. Most namely, it keeps breaking. I'm on my fifth unit in 3 years. Luckily it does have a 2 year warranty and Philips/Norelco has been terrific at replacing them. But, still, this continually breaking is a problem. I think this is mostly due to the cheap plastic build.

I also agree with another review in regards to the ON/OFF and Turbo buttons being in a bad location. Because these buttons are where the fingers naturally sit to hold the trimmer I'm constantly, unintentionally, turning the trimmer off. This is very annoying. And I too have had the unit change to a shorter setting during use. Also very annoying.

The brush is very soft, soft enough to use on your face or your more sensitive spots, but still stiff enough to clean those callouses on your feet. The loofa side is soft enough not to be irritating on the skin, but it is very small AND someone thought it was a good idea to put a rope loop sticking through the loofa so you actually end up trying to scrub your body with the rope instead of the loofa. VERY annoying. They should have found a better place for that rope loop - like attached to the back of the handle. And the neck of the handle is built at a pretty severe curve, makes it so that if you try to scrub yourself with the loofa you will just smack yourself with the bent part of the plastic handle instead.

The brush side is pretty good and the plastic handle is comfortable and solid, but I'm tall and also disabled with limited range of motion in my shoulders... so for me the handle is too short by almost a foot. That, combined with the bad design decisions they made on the loofa side... this is one of the worst shower sticks I've seen.

When this first arrived, I was going to open the amazon packaging and I could smell a strong, medicine like scent. So, I immediately thought that it must have broken in transit. Once I opened the amazon shipping package, there was a box inside. There wasn’t anything all over the box, so I opened it, and inside was a glass bottle completely intact. I couldn’t understand why the scent was so strong if the bottle was intact. Then, I thought if I can smell it that strong now, I wonder how it’ll be using it. The scent of the packaging had such a strong medicine kind of pepper smell, it was really overpowering.

I replaced the cutter head at 12 months, but found out my old head still cut at about 90% - 95% of the new one, so the cutters are durable. The bad news is that the razor I bought to replace this one costs a lot less than I paid for the cutting head! text:
I’ve got the KXAMELIE mountain green short nail set. It’s a lovely hunter green, as pictured, but that’s about it. They’re not nearly as nice or thick as advertised. I don’t think they’re UV gel, just plastic.

The instructions are vague and unhelpful for beginners and you have to carefully peel off a sticker just to read them. I really wanted to like these nails, yet the glue tab system is a real pain in the neck! You have to get it on your nail, wrestle off the plastic cover, hold under a hair dryer until it looks wet or your skin feels like it’s gonna fall off, pop the nail on and hope it’s straight, and then repeat over and over and over. I guess I could’ve used liquid glue but I didn’t have any handy that day so…. I will say the glue stickers were stronger than I was expecting. They remind me of those little glue dots you get on stuff in the mail sometimes.

My biggest beef with these is that they all come with jagged edges on the ends(however they were manufactured I presume) that snag on things and zero instructions on how to file or trim them. Just a tiny cardboard file tossed in.

Also, beware if you have small hands, which I do, so I’ve run into this problem a lot. The nail sizes are either a bit too small or too big. There’s no good in-between and you can see the gaps in the pictures. I prefer a little gapping to the plastic overlap digging into my skin. Trust me, they looked worse in person, tho. I was kind of embarrassed to wear them at work.

Overall, better than dollar store quality but not by much. Not for beginners due to the hassle. I wouldn’t try again as they only held up for a day. It was the rare color that lured me in.

title: Much Room for Improvement
text:
I didn't buy from this Amazon vendor and am still in the installation process. This is what I feel about this product so far:
1) The funtions and the price seems very attactive. However, there are many design issue made the installation process not pleasant.
2) The installation manual, as expected through preview, is horrible. There are many key steps not clearly stated. I have to figured them out myself and it took me long time to do so.
3) The design is not space saving. The hardwares are behind the glass panels which demand space. Although it claims to be standard 60X32. The space inside the enclosure is much smaller than that because of the hardware behind the glass panels. This, by the way, is not clearly explained, and I concerned about not having enough bathroom space to host it. I had to put the frame up to understand that it requires 60X32 finished space to host the unit. Essentially treat it like a washer/dryer.
4) The drainage design is not American standard, and I was told it's European. The drainage pipe is only 1 1/2" (American uses 2" pipe) and no clear instruction in the menu on drainage hookup or choices of rough in preparation. The flexible drainage pipe looks cheap and I am not sure how long it will last before leaking.

I'll update you once the unit is finished and tested. Oeverall, the price seems really attractive. I recommend to have an experienced guy, which is hard to find, to put it together.

The contractor just got the installation 95% done. The unit looks beautiful. Everything works. I didn't regret the purchase, and feel the manufacturer should improve the product, especially installation manual, to deserve more stars.

title: Some nice items, but disappointing quality for toenail clippers
text:
This is a comprehensive set of nail cutting/trimming/maintaining tools. The standard clipper is very nice -- solid, sharp, and well up to the task of handling fingernails and lighter toenails. The various tools are also of decent quality.

What's not so good is the toenail clippers. It has a rather lightweight feel to it compared with other clippers I've used. The short handles make it less comfortable to use than other clippers. More importantly, the spring mechanism failed within the first couple of minutes of use. It uses two leaf style springs that push the jaws apart. The problem is with how they attach to the handle. There are two little prongs for each spring that fit into two little holes in the handle. For mine, the pins are too short to make a solid connection, so one falls (or rather, jumps) out no matter how many times I've tried to seat it properly into the handle (see photo). It can be used without the spring, but it's quite cumbersome to do so. Given the importance of the toenail clipper to the overall usefulness of the kit, I see this as a 2 star product.

If the springs were better it would be 4 stars since, even when properly functioning, the clippers are not as easy to use as others, but warrant 4 stars given the low cost compared with better quality clippers.

title: A Little TOO Old School for Me
text:
The PROS: This product does exactly what it says it will: it stiffens the hair so that it will stand up straight, which is why it is ideal for Flat Tops. It is not heavily perfumed, like a lot of hair products on the market these days. It has a very slight fragrance in the jar, but once you put it in your hair it is practically undetectable. Even though the jar is small, it will last a long time because you only need to use a little bit at a time.

The CONS: Because this product is petroleum-based, it is very heavy and sticky. In fact, it has almost the same consistency as Vasaline..perhaps a little bit thicker. Shampooing it out of your hair is like trying to clean up an oil spill. It will stay in your hair for a few days unless you use dish detergent (DAWN) to wash it out with.
Also, if your hair is more than about 1 1/2 inches in length, it will make your hair look greasy and stringy. As the label states, it is best suited for very short hair.

title: Lovely pampering skincare, frustrating packaging
text:
This product is a perfect example of a good product compromised by packaging. Each of the four pampering products was lovely: the body butter was rich and moisturizing without leaving the skin feeling greasy, the scrub had a good texture that never scratched or left skin dried out; the body wash felt great and cleansing, and even the bath salts, the weakest offering in the bunch, left the water pleasantly scented with a fresh, sparkling pineapple scent. Indeed, if you are a pineapple fan the combination of all these products is heavenly.

But the creams and potions are difficult to extract from their packaging! Instead of bottles or pots, a sealed envelope is used, similar to the ones you might purchase loose tea in. It takes up less room and weighs less than traditional packaging, so this option is very environmentally friendly. I was able to squeeze the body cream and body wash out in a manner similar to pushing toothpaste out of a tube, but I wasn’t able to get everything. The bath salts shook right out, so that wasn’t bad. But oh, the scrub! I loved the texture of the scrub but it was impossible to get out. It wouldn’t squeeze out and it was too sticky to pour, so I had to try and reach in and scoop it out with my fingertips. I gave up after using less than half of it because so much of the scrub got pushed into the deep corners of the envelope that I couldn’t get to it.

I recommend skipping this travel option and buying full-sized products instead. They’re great to use and very moisturizing for the skin - I would rate most of them 4 or 5 stars if not for the travel packaging.

title: Not As Good As Previous Norelco Models. Not For Anyone With a Mustache or Beard
text:
I have been using Norelco shavers for 30 years at least. This was my 4th model of Norelco shaver. I have been using this shaver about 6 months. For the first time I am very disappointed in a Norelco product and I will purchase another brand soon.

The trimmer is nearly non-functional. With the old Norelco products, the trimmers worked very well and I would only occassionally have to pull out a special purpose mustache/beard trimmer to perform maintenance on my goatee. With this new 1090, I have to use a separate trimmer all the time. The location of the trimmer makes it very difficult to see where it is placed so I can't use it safely to keep the goatee whisker length in check without risking overcutting it. And the trimemr blades barely protrude from the body of the shaver which makes it nearly impossible to get the trimmer on a lone stray whisker. Now I have to to travel with 2 shavers.

Every other usage requires the shaver to be rinsed out. When travelling I have to keep the shaver in a travel case. This forces me to regularly dry the shaver with the hotel blow-dryer before I use it because it isn't yet dry from the previous day's cleaning. Every day I am either cleaning it or drying it. A real pain.

I will admit that it is light, feels good in the hand, and shaves well if you use it every day. If you skip shaving for a few days it takes many passes before it shaves all the long whiskers. I typically need to use a trimmer to cut some strays down before finishing off.

This product is not effective for anyone with mustaches or beards or someone that skips a day or two on a regular basis. Given how expensive it is, you would be well advised to find a different product to purchase.

At the end of the day, it didn't feel like a high end, high grade sunscreen but rather like any old sunscreen you can get from the store. Save your money and try something more water/essence like. I traded this for the Missha soft finish and am MUCH happier.

title: Not as good as past Norelco shavers
text:
I was initially disappointed in this razor and continue to be disappointed. I've used Norelco's for many years. This one doesn't stack up to the others I had owned.

Reasons why:
Cheap Plastic
Poor Performance

When I received the razor, I thought: It look cools, but felt like a cheap knockoff in my hand.

The motor doesn't seem to have much power. If I go a day or two without shaving, I have to shave three to four times to clean up areas it misses.

I still own my old 90's vintage Norelco. I am tempted to buy it new blades and use it over this razor. Before I do that, I will buy an upgraded Norelco and try it. If the new razor doesn't measure up to the old 90's era razor, then I will try buying a different brand.
